# Secret-value shapes for scripts/secret-dump-compare.py (cadence-hooks#1662).
# Every row starts with a class and a space:
#   P  the value lands in the command's own output (may move ASK -> BLOCK)
#   C  the value goes to a consumer (must not move)
#   Q  nothing reaches the output, or no value is read (must not move)
# Item names and references are made up. Blank lines and `#` lines are skipped.
# A `⏎` in a row is a newline, so a row can hold a heredoc.
# The everyday rows come from scripts/testdata/confirm-tier-commands.txt.

# --- printed: the tool's own output ---
P op read op://v/i/f
P op read "op://v/item name/credential"
P op read op://v/i/f >&2
P op read op://v/i/f > /dev/stdout
P op read op://v/i/f -o /dev/stdout
P op read op://v/i/f 2>/dev/null
P op read --no-newline op://v/i/f
P op item get db --fields password --reveal
P op item get db --reveal --format json
P security find-generic-password -s svc -a me -w
P security find-generic-password -ws svc
P security find-internet-password -s host -w
P sudo security find-generic-password -s svc -w
P echo start; security find-generic-password -s x -w && echo done
P cd /repo && op read op://v/i/f
P kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.data.token}'
P kubectl -n prod get secrets/app -ojsonpath={.data.k}
P kubectl get secret s --template='{{.data.p}}'
P vault kv get -field=password secret/x
P vault read -field=value secret/x
P aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x --query SecretString --output text
P aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1
P aws ssm get-parameter --name /x --with-decryption
P aws configure get aws_secret_access_key
P az keyvault secret show --vault-name v -n x
P az account get-access-token
P gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=x
P gcloud auth print-access-token
P heroku auth:token
P pass show x
P pass db
P gopass show db
P bw get password item
P lpass show --password item
P doppler secrets get KEY --plain

# --- printed: a substitution an argument printer prints, or a script ---
P echo $(op read op://v/i/f)
P echo "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
P echo -n "token: $(op read op://v/i/f)"
P printf "%s\n" "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
P echo `pass show x`
P sudo echo "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
P "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
P sh -c 'pass show x'
P bash -c 'op read op://v/i/f'
P eval 'vault kv get -field=p secret/x'
P bash -c 'echo "$(op read op://v/i/f)"'

# --- consumer: a pipe into another program ---
C op read op://v/i/token | gh auth login --with-token
C op read op://v/i/f | docker login -u me --password-stdin registry.example
C security find-generic-password -s svc -w | docker login -u me --password-stdin
C security find-generic-password -s svc -w | pbcopy
C op read op://v/i/f | pbcopy
C op read op://v/i/f | tr -d '\n' | pbcopy
C op read op://v/i/f | wc -c
C op read op://v/i/f | grep -q expected
C op read op://v/i/f | base64 -d > key.bin
C kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 -d
C kubectl get secret s -o json | jq -r .data.p | base64 -d
C bash -c 'op read op://v/i/f' | pbcopy

# --- consumer: a substitution used as an argument, assignment or prefix ---
C X=$(security find-generic-password -s svc -w); echo $X
C export GH_TOKEN="$(op read op://v/i/t)"
C GH_TOKEN="$(op read op://v/i/t)" gh api user
C TOKEN=$(op read op://v/i/f) gh api user
C env T="$(op read op://v/i/f)" npm publish
C curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $(op read op://v/i/f)" https://api.example
C curl -fsS -u "me:$(security find-generic-password -s svc -w)" https://api.example
C psql "postgres://u:$(pass show db)@h/db"
C mysql -p"$(pass show db)" -e 'select 1'
C ssh h "echo $(op read op://v/i/f)"
C gh secret set API_KEY --body "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
C docker login --password-stdin <<< "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
C gh auth login --with-token < <(op read op://v/i/f)
C cat <(pass show x)
C echo "$(op read op://v/i/f)" | docker login --password-stdin
C echo "$(op read op://v/i/f)" > token.txt
C echo $(op read op://v/i/f | sha256sum)
C $HOME/bin/tool --token "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
C "$TOOL" login -p "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
C ${KUBECTL:-kubectl} create secret generic s --from-literal=p="$(op read op://v/i/f)"
C printf -v TOKEN '%s' "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
C echo hi 2>"$(op read op://v/i/f)"
C echo <(op read op://v/i/f)
C docker login -u me --password-stdin <<EOF⏎$(op read op://v/i/f)⏎EOF
C cat <<EOF | docker login --password-stdin⏎$(op read op://v/i/f)⏎EOF
C kubectl apply -f - <<EOF⏎kind: Secret⏎  pw: $(op read op://v/i/f)⏎EOF
C cat > config.yml <<EOF⏎pw: $(op read op://v/i/f)⏎EOF
C psql <<-EOF⏎ALTER ROLE u PASSWORD '$(pass show db)';⏎EOF
C gh secret set K <<EOF⏎$(op read op://v/i/f)⏎EOF
C cat <<EOF⏎$(op read op://v/i/f)⏎EOF
C echo "T=$(op read op://v/i/f)">>.env
C printf '%s' "$(op read op://v/i/f)">.env
C op read op://v/i/f>token.txt
C op read op://v/i/f>/dev/null
C op read op://v/i/f 2>&1>/dev/null
C op read op://v/i/f | tee .env
C { op read op://v/i/f; } > token.txt
C ( op read op://v/i/f ) | pbcopy

# --- quiet: the value goes to a file or a hash, or nothing is read ---
Q op read op://v/i/f > token.txt
Q op read --out-file token.txt op://v/i/f
Q op read -o token.txt op://v/i/f
Q op read op://v/i/f | sha256sum
Q security find-generic-password -s svc -w | shasum -a 256
Q security find-generic-password -s svc -w > /dev/null
Q kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 -d | shasum
Q op run --env-file app.env -- npm test
Q op run -- gh api user
Q op inject -i config.tpl -o config.yml
Q op item get db --fields username
Q op item get "Example Token" --fields label=token
Q op item list --vault Example
Q op vault list
Q op whoami
Q op signin
Q security find-generic-password -s svc
Q security unlock-keychain
Q kubectl get secret app -o yaml
Q kubectl get pods -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'
Q vault kv get secret/x
Q aws configure get region
Q pass ls
Q echo 'op read op://v/i/f'
Q git commit -m 'op read op://x'
Q rg 'op read' src
